I will do it the way I know from the field, not from talking. My land is only 4.1 mu, so every bag of fertilizer is money out of my pocket. I will start from what I did before and what I see working around me. For wheat and maize, I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steady food-and-cash pattern here, and I have well water, so I do not want to leave yield on the table. I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than watch the crop turn weak. I will leave a smaller piece for cotton, because cotton takes more looking after and more spraying, and with people working off-farm I cannot watch too much cotton every day. On wheat I will use more nitrogen because if the wheat is thin in spring, the harvest drops fast. On maize I will feed it enough after wheat stubble so it grows fast in summer. Cotton I will not make too large, but I will still feed it and spray it more times because worms and sucking pests can ruin it quick. I will plough or rotary till where I need a clean seedbed, and after wheat I will keep maize simple and fast so I do not lose moisture and planting time.
